points: This carryover audit supplements only G2 and G3; G0/G4/G5/G1 are inherited from the existing candidate record and were not re-adjudicated.

A real Chrome session read the complete first two US-English Google result pages. Page one contains one exact Java Images-service migration guide, App Engine-to-Cloud Run forums, two general Java migration codelabs, a general migration overview, an independent article, a product homepage, and an unrelated deployment forum; page two drops into general migration forums, blogs, a Python Images-service guide, Medium, and a generic migration helper.

G2=pass: forums, codelabs, documentation inner pages, small articles, and older generic material occupy substantial space; there is no video, wiki, major-media, or strong-brand-homepage takeover, and page two establishes a quality cliff for the exact Java Images-service task.

The exact Google Cloud Java guide is a complete implementation: it covers limitations and roles, deploys the prebuilt authenticated Cloud Run image-processing service, grants IAM, updates Maven dependencies and appengine-web.xml environment flags, redeploys App Engine, and verifies both services in logs.

The two Java codelabs containerize a general App Engine application with Jib or Buildpacks but do not replace the legacy Images-service backend. The page-two Python guide solves the same service migration in a different language, while general migration articles and the helper do not cover the Images-service routing contract.
G3=pass: only one free exact Java App Engine Images-service to Cloud Run implementation is stably visible across the two pages, below the veto threshold of two.
This is not veto_window_bet because no second already-built exact Java implementation was found merely awaiting indexing.
Window estimate is weeks, expiring 2026-09-20. The exact Java guide is newly updated, while general App Engine migration content and a Python sibling already create nearby competition.

Invalidation conditions: a second free end-to-end Java Images-service migration guide becomes stably visible; Google publishes a Java codelab or sample that mirrors the exact migration; the prebuilt image-processing container, SDK version, or APPENGINE_IMAGES_SERVICE_ENDPOINT routing contract changes.
Caveat: Chrome used a signed-in Google session with gl=us, hl=en, pws=0; the result footer reported that results were not personalized, while safe=active and ssui=on were appended by Google.
